scenes.title: Create another attempt while trailing late
scenes.objective: Assess a late attacking choice without declaring a guaranteed scoring play.
scenes.briefing: Navy trails by one with 32 seconds left and has five skaters on the ice. YOU control at the puck-side point. F1 is near the net, F2 is across the high slot and D2 is the other high player. Navy’s goalie, omitted from this selected-player view, remains in net; no extra attacker is assumed. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing explicitly excludes a goalie pull, avoiding an unstated manpower assumption.

Navy trails by one with 32 seconds left and has five skaters on the ice. YOU control at the puck-side point. F1 is near the net, F2 is across the high slot and D2 is the other high player. The goalie remains in net; no extra attacker is assumed.

questions.prompt: Is an extra attacker part of this stated setup?

options.text: No Navy players are near the net
No, Navy has five skaters and its goalie remains in net
Yes, Navy has six skaters

questions.explanation: The briefing explicitly excludes a goalie pull, avoiding an unstated manpower assumption.

questions.prompt: With 32 seconds left, which two current pressure relationships matter when comparing F1 near the net and F2 across the high slot?

options.text: Gold 1 is nearer the direct line to F1 than the line to F2
Gold 3 is nearer the direct line to F2 than the line to F1
Gold 5 is closer to F1 than Gold 2 is

questions.explanation: The two connections face different defenders: Gold 1 near the F1 line and Gold 3 near the F2 line. Check whether either connection can create a feasible attempt in the remaining time; the static picture does not establish pass or shot timing.

questions.prompt: Arrange a time-aware attacking read.

options.text: Check the remaining clock and immediate lanes
Compare the available shot and connecting pass
Commit to a feasible attempt and support its next touch

questions.explanation: Checking the clock/lanes and comparing the shot against a connecting pass can overlap as YOU scan; only committing to the attempt and supporting its next touch has to come last, once those reads are in. The still setup cannot validate travel times or scoring probability.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a more central point angle.
questions.explanation: The reference changes the shot and pass routes. It may consume time, so it is an illustration rather than a prescribed late-game skate.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 lunges into the shot lane and F2 becomes visible. What should be considered?

options.text: The unchanged shot lane from before the lunge
An automatic hold until the clock expires
A quick checked connection to F2

questions.explanation: The new cue can favour a connection, but the available time and F2’s preparation still matter.

questions.prompt: Why is “get a shot” incomplete feedback in this final-minute scene?
questions.explanation: Explain route, traffic, time and possible next possession; more attempts are not identical chances.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate while trailing late?

options.text: We need a chance; check the lane before forcing it
The deficit makes every shot correct
F2 stays the preferred option even if Gold closes the route

questions.explanation: The call acknowledges the deficit while preserving a scan before risk.

questions.prompt: Which two updates support a remaining chance?

options.text: Gold 1 commits to the carrier
F2 or F3 becomes reachable
The clock alone creates a lane

questions.explanation: Defender commitment and support access create the attacking branch.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a more central point angle toward F2.
questions.explanation: The example is nearer the middle and farther from Gold 1. Check the changed passing route, traffic and remaining time; the point does not establish an open lane.

questions.prompt: Gold blocks F2 but leaves F3 wide. Explain your next read.
questions.explanation: Recheck F3 and the net-side lane, then choose a pass or carry only if it remains reachable; the deficit does not remove that condition.

scenes.title: Join the second wave only after checking possession
scenes.objective: Assess an offensive activation while keeping a stated covering defender.
scenes.briefing: F1 has recovered the puck and carries into the neutral zone. YOU are the supporting defender; D2 stays deeper by agreement. F2 is ahead and Gold 3 is recovering near YOU. The drill permits an activation only after secure possession and available support are checked. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing assigns deeper cover to D2 before the activation is considered.

F1 has recovered the puck and carries into the neutral zone. YOU are the supporting defender; D2 stays deeper by agreement. F2 is ahead and Gold 3 is recovering near YOU. The drill permits an activation only after secure possession and available support are checked.

questions.prompt: Which defender has the explicitly stated deeper-cover role?

options.text: Gold 3
D2
YOU

questions.explanation: The briefing assigns deeper cover to D2 before the activation is considered.

questions.prompt: Choose two checks for joining the attack.

options.text: F1’s quality of possession
The idea that every recovery requires both defenders to go
Whether D2 and recovering pressure support the decision

questions.explanation: Activation is a conditional choice; the source principle does not erase risk.

questions.prompt: Arrange an activation assessment.

options.text: Confirm controlled possession
Check covering support and Gold 3
Join or hold according to the updated picture

questions.explanation: Confirming controlled possession and checking covering support/Gold 3 can overlap as YOU skate; only joining or holding has to come last, once both reads are in. The routine assumes the stated cover plan and still needs realistic timing.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a second-wave supporting lane.
questions.explanation: The example is behind F2 and F3 but slightly ahead of carrier F1, in a different lane. Recheck D2’s cover and Gold 3; arrival timing and a passing window are not established.

questions.prompt: Imagine F1 bobbles the puck before YOU join the second wave. Which Gold player is currently closest to both YOU and F1, making that pressure especially relevant to the hold-or-join decision?

options.text: Gold 1
Gold 2
Gold 3

questions.explanation: Gold 3 is near both the supporting defender and F1. Check the actual puck contest and D2’s cover before continuing the activation; a bobble alone does not establish Gold possession.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a useful second wave from leaving the play without cover?
questions.explanation: Discuss secure possession, D2’s role, pressure and a reachable support lane.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate before joining the second wave?

options.text: F1 has control and D2 is behind me; call if either changes
The attack makes cover unnecessary
F2 owns the puck

questions.explanation: The message names carrier and cover, the two conditions for activation.

questions.prompt: Which two changes require reassessing the activation?

options.text: F1 loses control
D2 leaves the deeper cover
F2 stays wide

questions.explanation: Possession and cover determine whether the second wave remains responsible.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a second-wave lane behind F1, separate from F3.
questions.explanation: The example stays behind F1 and separate from F3. Check D2’s deeper cover and Gold 3’s recovery before continuing; no open pass is guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Gold 3 accelerates as F1 bobbles. What is your new priority?
questions.explanation: Recover or hold the cover first, then re-read F1 and F2. The earlier activation plan is stale.

scenes.title: Prepare the first touch but keep a second option
scenes.objective: Compare a prepared first-touch play with the need to update a changed lane.
scenes.briefing: D1 has released a firm pass toward YOU in the neutral zone. The puck is in transit. F1 is the prepared forward option, but Gold 1 is closing that route. The coach asks YOU to scan before reception; a one-touch pass is permitted, not required. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The loose marker represents the explicitly stated pass in transit.

questions.prompt: What is the puck doing according to the briefing?

options.text: Travelling from D1 toward YOU
Already controlled by F1
Already sitting still at YOUR feet

questions.explanation: The loose marker represents the explicitly stated pass in transit.

questions.prompt: While D1’s pass is still travelling toward YOU, which two current receiver-pressure relationships belong in the pre-scan?

options.text: Gold 1 is closer to F1 than Gold 2 is
Gold 2 is closer to F2 than Gold 1 is
Gold 3 is closer to YOU than Gold 2 is

questions.explanation: F1 has Gold 1 nearby, and F2 has Gold 2 nearby. Prepare alternatives using those pressures, then update the arriving puck quality and passing lines before choosing a redirect or a controlling touch.

questions.prompt: Arrange a prepared-reception routine.

options.text: Scan the forward option before arrival
Update the lane and puck quality
Redirect or control according to what remains available

questions.explanation: Repeated scans can overlap with receiving; extra control is not automatically an error.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a different receiving angle toward F1 and F2.
questions.explanation: The example changes both forward routes and moves farther from the current loose puck. Whether the pass reaches this new point in time is not established; YOU do not yet control it.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 closes F1 completely as the pass arrives. What might be appropriate?

options.text: Pretend the pre-scan picture cannot change
Control or use another checked option
One-touch into F1’s closed lane by rule

questions.explanation: The latest cue should override a stale preplanned pass.

questions.prompt: How can a player prepare early without committing too early?
questions.explanation: Describe a provisional option, renewed scanning and an alternative if pressure or the arriving puck changes.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate before the loose pass arrives?

options.text: I am preparing a touch; call if F1 or F2 becomes covered
The planned spot guarantees the reception
Both support lanes remain available after Gold closes one route

questions.explanation: The message prepares early while leaving the first touch conditional.

questions.prompt: Which two changes affect the first touch?

options.text: Gold 1 closes F1
F2 remains reachable
The intended puck spot stays current after it drifts

questions.explanation: Pressure and support affect the actual loose puck; the intended spot is no longer enough.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare another approach to the arriving pass.
questions.explanation: The example moves farther from the current puck and closer to Gold 1. Recheck the pass trajectory and pressure before trying this point; it does not guarantee reception or an open outlet.

questions.prompt: Gold closes F1 completely as the puck arrives. Explain your branch.
questions.explanation: Protect the first touch and check F2 or a reset. Do not treat the covered target as the only continuation.

scenes.title: Manage a lead in the final minute
scenes.objective: Use the stated clock and score to weigh controlled possession against a safe reset.
scenes.briefing: Navy leads 3–2 with one minute left. Navy attacks the Gold net. YOU own the puck near centre; F1 is wide support, F2 is higher, and Gold pressures from both sides. The score and clock are explicit practice conditions.
cues: Navy leads 3–2 with one minute left.
F1 and F2 are visible support options.

options.text: Navy trails 2–3
Navy leads 3–2 with one minute left
The clock is not stated

questions.explanation: The briefing states a one-goal Navy lead with one minute remaining.

questions.prompt: Which two cues affect the possession objective?

options.text: The stated lead and clock
F1 and F2's reachable support
The lead means every forward option is wrong

questions.explanation: The score and time shape risk, while support determines whether possession can be kept.

questions.prompt: Arrange a late-possession read.

options.text: Scan pressure and support
Protect or move the puck to a reachable option
Re-check whether the next lane remains safe

questions.explanation: The lead informs risk, but the actual support and pressure still decide the next action.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare routes toward F1 and F2.
questions.explanation: The example moves closer to F1 and F2, but also closer to Gold 1. Check pressure and both routes before treating either as a controlled outlet.

questions.prompt: With one minute left and a one-goal lead, which current forward passing line stays farther from Gold 2?

options.text: The direct line from YOU to F1
The direct line from YOU to F2

questions.explanation: Gold 2 is much nearer the F2 line than the F1 line. That favours examining F1 as a controlled outlet, but Gold 1, Gold 3 and F1’s receiving space still need checking before a pass.

questions.prompt: Explain a sensible risk tradeoff without saying “never attack with a lead.”
questions.explanation: With a one-goal lead and one minute, value possession and support, but use a forward lane when it is clearly reachable and pressure leaves it available.

scenes.title: Protect the backdoor during rotation
scenes.objective: Exchange a low defensive responsibility while keeping the backdoor lane covered.
scenes.briefing: Gold attacks Navy’s left net with four skaters against three in this penalty-kill example. Gold 1 controls behind the goal line and Gold 2 is across the low slot. YOU are on the side opposite the puck; D1 is on the puck side. The drill assigns YOU the low threat until a teammate confirms coverage. Gold 3 may cut inward in a later hypothetical.
cues: Gold 1 has the puck below the line.
Gold 2 is across the low slot.
YOU and D1 share a changing inside responsibility.

Gold 2's route to the backdoor

options.text: Identify puck and backdoor threat
Communicate the low exchange

questions.prompt: Imagine Gold 3 cuts inward while Gold 2 stays at the shown spot. No teammate has confirmed a coverage handoff. Under this drill’s assignment, which attacker remains YOUR low responsibility as YOU call out the new threat?

Gold 3

questions.explanation: Keep responsibility for Gold 2 until a teammate confirms the exchange, while communicating Gold 3’s new threat. If the handoff is confirmed or the attack changes again, update the coverage; this drill condition does not prescribe one skating route.

questions.prompt: Which low-slot passing threat should YOU track before exchanging coverage?
questions.explanation: Gold 2 starts across the low slot from carrier Gold 1. If Gold 3 cuts inward, update the threats and confirm the teammate exchange; a pass or coverage outcome is not guaranteed.
